facts.fact: The telecoms regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali (AMRTP) and Niger signed a cooperation convention creating the Conseil des regulateurs du Sahel, covering harmonised rules, free roaming, border spectrum coordination and joint positions in the ITU; the article gives no signing date, so its published date 2026-09-26 is used.

facts.fact: Mali's minister told the Council of Ministers that Mali took part in the 7th ordinary Plenipotentiary Conference of the African Telecommunications Union, held 23 to 24 July 2026 in Abuja.

At the ATU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abuja (23 to 24 July 2026) Mali was re-elected a member of the ATU Administrative Council for the 2027-2031 term; the communique gives no more exact election date.

facts.fact: Mali's Minister of Communication and Digital Economy met the Smart Africa Alliance director general on the sidelines of MWC 2026 in Barcelona and discussed skills, fibre links with neighbours and hosting the next Transform Africa Summit; talks only, no agreement signed.

Mali's digital minister took part in the opening of the fourth SIPEN-UEMOA digital economy fair in Ouagadougou and delivered the address on behalf of the AES Confederation's digital ministers; no agreement was signed, a Declaration of Ouagadougou was only anticipated.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports on 26 October 2026 that Mali reached roaming agreements with Benin and Togo in December 2023, and Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed an agreement under the Confederation of Sahel States in November 2024.

leFaso.net, relaying a Burkina Faso ministry release, reports that digital ministers and experts of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, members of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), met in Ouagadougou on 3-5 November 2026 to finalise digital cooperation documents.
Sidwaya reports Mali's delegation took part in the AES workshop that finalised the digital deliverables of the Year II roadmap on 5 November 2026, 16 of 18 deliverables being final.
In September 2026 the telecom and postal regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed in Ouagadougou a convention creating the Council of Sahel Regulators.

Startup Medias reports the AES digital roadmap, 16 of 18 deliverables finalised, was adopted in Ouagadougou on 5 November 2026 by delegations of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, the Malian delegation head presenting the tally.

note: Nothing on African regional digital bodies.

facts.fact: Maliweb reports that Mali's regulator AMRTP hosted the Alliance of Sahel States' second coordination meeting on military frequencies in border areas in Bamako, 2-4 November 2026, with Burkina Faso and Niger delegations.

Maliweb says a convention of 25 September 2026 between the regulators of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger created the Council of Sahel Regulators, after a coordination agreement signed in Ouagadougou on 21 November 2025 covering cybersecurity and roaming.
Niger's regulator director general says AES free roaming among Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger was already operational before the regulators' convention was signed on 25 September 2026.
Ecofin Agency reports Senegal's regulator ARTP signed a roaming memorandum of understanding with its Malian counterpart on 11 December 2025, effective 1 March 2026.

note: The agreement is not yet in effect; it starts 1 March 2026.

facts.fact: Regulators of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso signed a memorandum of understanding on free roaming among Alliance of Sahel States members in Niamey, reported by Le Sahel (ONEP).

facts.fact: Mali's minister Alhamdou Ag Ilyene took part in the Alliance of Sahel States ministerial session in Ouagadougou on 27 November 2026 that validated a draft framework convention on digital and postal cooperation.

note: Only a draft convention was validated; no signature or act in effect stated.

facts.fact: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed the AES framework convention on cooperation in digital and postal matters (infrastructure sharing, connectivity, cybersecurity, e-government, AI) in Ouagadougou on 27 November 2026, per a ministry release carried by Wakat Sera.
